claims.claim: 200 small writes a second is modest for Spring MVC; I expect this to fit on the single vCPU
claims.measured: java-spring: 7,668 req/s single-row Postgres query at 100% CPU; java-spring-vt 12,731 req/s
claims.why: One CPU handled about 38 times the 200 req/s target, so calling the load modest and expecting it to fit matches the data.

claims.claim: Memory is the tightest limit; the JVM has to share 512 MB, and a mis-sized heap gets the process OOM-killed
claims.measured: java-spring peak memory: 491 MB (I/O wait), 499 MB (single query), 500 MB (20 queries) in a 512 MB container; CPU need at 200 req/s is only about 3% of one core
claims.why: Spring Boot peaked within about 12 MB of the 512 MB limit while CPU had large headroom, so memory really is the binding limit.

claims.claim: Go or Rust have the best footprint
claims.about: go-gin, go-nethttp, rust-actix, rust-axum vs java-spring
claims.measured: Go 7–16 MB peak, 2 MB idle; Rust 3–10 MB peak, 1 MB idle; java-spring 220–500 MB peak, 134 MB idle
claims.why: Go and Rust are among the smallest measured, roughly 30 to 100 times smaller than Spring Boot.

claims.claim: The footprint savings of Go/Rust aren't needed for 200 writes a second
claims.measured: java-spring 7,668 req/s on single-row DB, peak 499 MB within 512 MB
claims.why: Spring Boot's measured throughput and memory both fit the 200 req/s, 512 MB requirement, though memory is close to the limit.

claims.claim: Node.js has less performance headroom than Spring on one vCPU
claims.measured: Single-row DB: express 9,034, fastify 9,423 vs java-spring 7,668 req/s; plaintext: express 17,601, fastify 40,730 vs 13,653; Node peak memory 55–77 MB vs Spring 220–500 MB
claims.why: On the DB-write-like and plaintext tests both Node servers beat Spring MVC, and they use far less memory, so the claim points the wrong way for this workload.

claims.claim: Python has less performance headroom than Spring on one vCPU
claims.measured: Single-row DB: fastapi 3,706, flask 1,529–2,119 vs java-spring 7,668 req/s
claims.why: Every Python variant measured slower than Spring Boot on the DB and most other tests.

claims.claim: Using JdbcClient/JdbcTemplate instead of JPA/Hibernate saves memory and startup time
claims.why: Only one Spring data-access setup was measured, so JDBC and JPA can't be compared.

claims.claim: Quarkus or Micronaut are lighter than Spring
claims.why: Neither Quarkus nor Micronaut was benchmarked.

claims.claim: Spring Boot native image (GraalVM) cuts memory and startup time
claims.why: No native-image build was measured; only JVM Spring Boot, with 5.9–6.2 s start-up and 131–134 MB idle.

claims.claim: Use a single-CPU-friendly GC (Serial, or G1 with a small heap)
claims.why: The benchmark doesn't vary or report GC settings.

claims.claim: A shared reverse proxy or load balancer costs less than running nginx on the same small VM
claims.why: No setup with nginx running next to the app on the same machine was measured.
